subject: Annualize + Surge-pocket onramp: cadence, soft-throttle & ops playbook
messages:
From: Samir Khan <samir.k@cartstack.com>

Date: Fri, 6 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosted usage — annualize + surge pocket question

Hey Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo last week — CartStack's engineering and ML teams were impressed by the latency and the cost breakdown you shared. We're reaching the end of our current monthly commit and want to discuss an annualized path that gives us both predictable monthly throughput and a small surge pocket for holiday peaks.

High level asks from our side:
- Move from current 3M tokens/mo to a 9M tokens/mo annual commit (billed monthly)
- A 20% surge pocket for peak months (holiday window, Black Friday) that doesn't immediately trigger overage pricing
- A soft-throttle policy that preserves request-level latency SLOs but adds fair-use gating if we hit burst extremes

Can you share a short proposal and an ops playbook we can show to procurement and infra? Procurement will need MPA redlines and an expected billing cadence.

Samir
Samir Khan
Head of ML Infrastructure, CartStack

Samir — great to hear CartStack wants to annualize. I've attached a short proposal (CartStack_Annual_Proposal_v2.pdf) that lays out two options:

Option A (Conservative): 9M tokens/mo annual commit, 10% pre-approved surge, step-up pricing for >10% sustained growth
Option B (Aggressive + Surge-pocket): 9M tokens/mo annual commit, 20% surge pocket for three named months, soft-throttle policy and an agreed failover to a lower-cost compatible model if urgent capacity is hit

Operational notes (ops playbook highlights):
- Onramp cadence: 30-day pilot buffer, then monthly billing starts at the annualized rate
- Throttle behavior: burst window preserved for 95th pct requests; gating applies to non-critical batch jobs first
- Fallback model: we recommend enabling the quantized-compat variant to protect SLOs with lower per-token cost during peak fallback

I've looped in Lauren to confirm billing cadence and Grace for capacity sequencing. If procurement prefers, we can post the MPA redlines into DocuSign for signature.

Next steps:
1) We finalize Option B terms (if you confirm surge months and exact 3-month window).
2) Legal/Proc run redlines (we'll send MPA_redline.docx back to you).
3) Ops onboarding call to confirm routing and fallback policies.

Would Tuesday 11/10 10:00 PT work for an ops + procurement sync?

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer

Thanks — quick ops + billing notes from our side before the sync:

Billing / Finance (Lauren):
- We can annualize with monthly invoices at the committed rate. PO accepted. If CartStack wants a single annual invoice, we can accommodate with 2% admin fee for reconciliation.
- Surge-pocket usage will be drawn down from a named "surge bucket" first; any use beyond the bucket in a billing window will be billed at the published overage rate unless we pre-agree a temporary discounted overage during holiday months.

Capacity / Ops (Grace):
- To enable the 20% surge pocket safely we need: advance traffic window names (example: Nov 20–Dec 5, Dec 18–Jan 3, and one flex week in Q1).
- We'll stage the rollout: enable KV cache warm-up, pre-warm a subset of GPUs, and schedule a canary on the quantized-compat fallback path.
- For the soft-throttle, we propose the following fall-through order: non-interactive batch -> reduced token window for low-priority calls -> switch to fallback model. This preserves latency for interactive endpoints.

I've attached the MPA redlines the legal team typically requests (MPA_redline.docx). Karthik — if procurement confirms the three surge windows Samir suggested, we'll populate the redline and produce a DocuSign envelope.

Lauren Bishop
Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference

Karthik / Lauren / Grace — thanks for the proposal. Procurement (Maya here, cc'd Samir) — we reviewed Option B and are comfortable with the structure pending two clarifications:

1) Surge-pocket drawdown: please confirm how unused surge pocket is handled (rolls forward? expires after the annual cycle?).
2) Soft-throttle SLOs: we need a short operational SLA that guarantees <120ms p95 for interactive endpoints even during fallback; if that cannot be met, we want an agreed credit mechanism.

We will sign the MPA redline once you confirm those two points and provide the DocuSign link. We attached our PO (PO-67912) in procurement systems — please confirm final invoice cadence.

Maya Patel
Procurement Lead, CartStack
